page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 vCPUs backed by 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. Hardware allocation is dedicated, supported by 32 KB L1d cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. It provides 32.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU core. Instruction set features include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions. The server includes no local storage, requiring network-attached volumes, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No discrete GPUs are installed.

Performance across standardized synthetic benchmarks demonstrates balanced multi-core output alongside lower single-thread execution rates. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core testing and Geekbench multi-core scores, register within the middle 50% benchmark tier. Similarly, compiler workloads with Clang, ray tracing, text processing, and PassMark database operations exhibit average throughput performance. Single-threaded tasks, such as stress-ng single-core execution and single-threaded Gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25% performance bracket. Memory bandwidth testing shows mid-range throughput, with 88.67 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 45.93 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations reach 13.44 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 11.29 GB/sec.

From an architectural perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks that do not require high memory footprints per vCPU. The absence of local disk hardware reduces host hardware overhead, shifting storage configuration to external persistent block storage based on IOPS requirements. The primary tradeoff lies in single-threaded compute efficiency, as single-core execution metrics lag behind multi-threaded execution metrics.

The instance configuration is aligned with multi-threaded parallel workloads, CI/CD software compilation pipelines, web application servers, and microservice backend nodes. It is also suitable for distributed database nodes and batch data processing jobs where parallel CPU resources and standard memory capacity are required.
